Recovery round 3 (after_specify, 20261013T104606Z: iterate, 1 failure mode — irreducibility on C06): C06's text recast in the Spec 031 C06 sentence shape; the crosswalk location (data/crosswalks) stands in its boundary and in spec section 3.3. claims.text: Spec 032 verdicts state whether the registered PRED-2026-006 criterion is met on the withheld Harappa data.
claims.boundary: The licensed-conclusion boundary of every Spec 032 output. This claim governs what a verdict may mean. It does not govern how the trained set is built (C03), how the score is computed (C08), or how the outcome is recorded (C11). The verdict states the criterion outcome and nothing beyond that statement.
alternatives: A met criterion under Spec 032 licenses a conclusion about what the signs mean or about stability at other sites.
falsification_tests: One conclusion in a Spec 032 report that reads beyond the registered statement (a meaning, a mechanism, or another site) defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A met criterion under Spec 032 licenses a conclusion about what the signs mean or about stability at other sites.
metadata.verdict_rule: The verdict applies only to the registered statement: the share of CISI-trained INITIAL signs meeting the Harappa start-rate bar, on the withheld Harappa data.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C01 bounds what a verdict MEANS; C02 fixes the criterion the verdict applies; C08 fixes the computation that produces the share. A verdict computed correctly under C08 and judged under C02 still may not be read beyond C01. C01 governs conclusions; C11 governs the register record. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: PRED-2026-006 entry: the registered statement the verdict is bounded to
Design portfolio D-30: the bounded statement and its not-established list

claims.text: The registered success criterion is a share of at least 70 percent of the frozen trained INITIAL signs with a Harappa start rate of at least 0.40.
claims.boundary: The criterion claim. It fixes the two registered numbers (the 70 percent share; the 0.40 start-rate bar) exactly as registered on 2026-04-22. It does not fix how the trained set is obtained (C03), how signs map (C06), or how the share is computed (C08).
alternatives: A near-miss share under the registered numbers may be reported as confirmed under a softened band.
falsification_tests: One Spec 032 scoring that applies a threshold, a band, or an adjustment other than the registered pair (70 percent; 0.40) defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A near-miss share under the registered numbers may be reported as confirmed under a softened band.
metadata.verdict_rule: CONFIRMED exactly when the computed share is at least 70 percent; NOT CONFIRMED below it; no other verdict wording exists under this spec.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C02 fixes the criterion; C08 fixes the computation the criterion judges; C04 and C12 govern the closures that replace a verdict when the test cannot run. C02 states the bar; it does not state the share, and it does not soften when the share is close. C02 and C07 share the trained-set boundary: C02 fixes the bar over that set; C07 reports the mapped fraction of it, and C07's coverage statement neither lowers nor negates C02's bar.

claims.text: The trained INITIAL sign set is the set reconstructed from the recorded CISI Mohenjo-daro training lineage.
claims.boundary: The trained-set provenance claim. It governs where the sign set comes from (the recorded lineage of the global class stability check) and when it is fixed (before counting). It does not govern the closure that follows if reconstruction fails (C04) or the crosswalk that maps the set (C06).
alternatives: A freshly built INITIAL set from current data is an acceptable substitute for the recorded trained set.
falsification_tests: One scoring under Spec 032 whose sign set was built fresh, sampled, or altered after counting began defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A freshly built INITIAL set from current data is an acceptable substitute for the recorded trained set.
metadata.verdict_rule: The scored sign set is the recorded trained set, reconstructed and frozen at step 0; any other set is outside this spec.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C03 governs the set's provenance; C04 governs the failure of that provenance; C06 governs the mapping applied to the set once frozen. C03 requires reconstruction from the record; it does not itself judge whether the reconstruction succeeded. C03 and C05 state different facts: C03 is the set's provenance in the records; C05 is the training lineage's composition, and neither negates the other. C03 and C07 share the set boundary: C03 freezes the set; C07 reports the fraction of it the crosswalk carries, which presupposes C03's frozen set rather than contradicting it.

evidence.description: The recorded training lineage: global_class_stability.py produced the INITIAL class assignments and the 72.7 percent global figure
The recorded stability output the trained set is reconstructed from

claims.text: The study closes as CANNOT BE RUN AS WRITTEN when step 0.1 fails.
claims.boundary: The trained-set closure claim. It governs the single stated consequence of a step-0.1 failure. It does not govern the withholding closure (C05 carries the parallel rule for step 0.2) or the reporting of closures (C12).
alternatives: A failed reconstruction may be repaired by registering a similar set under the same PRED number.
falsification_tests: One run under Spec 032 that proceeds to a verdict after the trained set failed to reproduce defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A failed reconstruction may be repaired by registering a similar set under the same PRED number.
metadata.verdict_rule: On step-0.1 failure the study's outcome is the closure CANNOT BE RUN AS WRITTEN, recorded as itself; no verdict is issued.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C04 states the closure for a failed trained-set reconstruction; C03 states the reconstruction requirement it follows from; C12 states how closures are reported. C04 names one closure trigger; C05's verification carries the second trigger, and neither claim issues a verdict. C04 and C09 share the outcome boundary: when C04's closure fires, the outcome is the closure record; C09's descriptive table accompanies a computed outcome and neither supplies nor softens a closure.

evidence.description: Design D-30 step 0.1: the fail-closed outcome for the trained set
The register's own rule: a successor prediction requires a new PRED number under a new registration

claims.text: The INITIAL class assignments derive from CISI Mohenjo-daro training only.
claims.boundary: The withholding claim. It states the fact step 0.2 verifies: the training lineage is CISI Mohenjo-daro only. It records the corpus's prior unrelated exposure (Phases 281-293) as context to be stated openly at execution; exposure alone neither proves nor defeats the withholding. It does not govern the trained set's reconstruction (C03).
alternatives: Prior unrelated use of the Yajnadevam corpus by the program voids the withholding regardless of the training lineage.
falsification_tests: One record showing Harappa Yajnadevam sequences inside the INITIAL training lineage defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Prior unrelated use of the Yajnadevam corpus by the program voids the withholding regardless of the training lineage.
metadata.verdict_rule: Step 0.2 verifies the training lineage from the record; if the lineage cannot be verified as CISI Mohenjo-daro only, the study closes as CANNOT BE RUN AS WRITTEN (the rule C04 states for step 0).
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C05 states the withholding fact and its verification; C03 states the trained set's provenance (a different fact: which signs, from which records); C10 states the independence the verdict may claim once C05 is verified. C05 verified is what licenses C10's wording; C05 unverified closes the study. C05 and C08 share the data boundary: C05 verifies the training lineage; C08 computes on the withheld sequences. Training provenance and scoring data are different facts; neither negates the other.

evidence.description: PRED-2026-006 withheld-data line: Harappa-site Yajnadevam sequences held separate
The training lineage artifact: class assignments computed from the corpus analysis the register describes

claims.text: Sign identity under Spec 032 is built only from the existing crosswalk files.
claims.boundary: The sign-identity claim. It governs the mapping instrument (the existing published crosswalk files) and its fixing time (before counting). It does not govern the trained set itself (C03) or the treatment of signs the mapping cannot carry (C07).
alternatives: Sign identity may be settled case by case at counting time where the crosswalk is ambiguous.
falsification_tests: One scored sign whose identity was assigned outside the frozen crosswalk files defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Sign identity may be settled case by case at counting time where the crosswalk is ambiguous.
metadata.verdict_rule: Every scored sign's identity passes through the frozen crosswalk files; a mapping decided during counting is outside this spec.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C06 governs the mapping instrument; C07 governs the residue the instrument cannot map; C08 governs the computation that consumes the mapped signs. C06 fixes the instrument before counting; it does not report coverage, which is C07's statement. C06 and C07 are sequential, not opposed: C07's unmappable residue exists because C06's instrument is fixed, and reporting it does not contradict the fixing.

evidence.description: The Yajnadevam-to-Parpola crosswalk file the mapping is carried by
Design D-30 step 0.3: crosswalks fixed before counting

claims.text: Unmappable coverage above 20 percent of the trained set is stated in the verdict's first sentence.
claims.boundary: The coverage claim. It governs the residue of the mapping (C06): its counting, its label, and the first-sentence rule above 20 percent. It does not change the criterion (C02) or the denominator rule of the computation (C08 states the share over the trained set with this coverage stated).
alternatives: Unmappable signs may be dropped quietly, with coverage noted in an appendix.
falsification_tests: One Spec 032 outcome that omits the unmappable count, or that buries above-20-percent coverage below the first sentence, defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Unmappable signs may be dropped quietly, with coverage noted in an appendix.
metadata.verdict_rule: The outcome reports the unmappable count and share; above 20 percent the coverage leads the verdict text.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C07 governs coverage reporting; C06 governs the mapping that produces the residue; C02 governs the bar the share is judged against. C07 neither raises nor lowers the bar; it makes the mapped fraction visible wherever the verdict appears. C07 and C03 share the set boundary: C03 freezes the set whose mapped fraction C07 reports. C07 and C09 share the reporting boundary: C07's coverage statement leads the verdict; C09's table accompanies it as a separate descriptive statement, and neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Design D-30 step 0.3: the UNMAPPABLE rule and the 20 percent first-sentence rule

claims.text: The score is the share of frozen trained INITIAL signs with a Harappa start rate of at least 0.40 on the withheld Harappa sequences.
claims.boundary: The computation claim. It fixes the scored quantity (the share), its population (the frozen trained set of C03, mapped under C06), and its data (the withheld Harappa sequences only). It does not fix the bar the share is judged against (C02) or the descriptive table published with it (C09).
alternatives: The share may be adjusted for sequence-length composition differences between Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.
falsification_tests: One Spec 032 score computed on any data beyond the withheld Harappa sequences, or with any adjustment the registration does not state, defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: The share may be adjusted for sequence-length composition differences between Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.
metadata.verdict_rule: The computed share is the unadjusted registered quantity; composition is described alongside (C09's table and the outcome text), never adjusted into the share.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C08 fixes the computation; C02 fixes the criterion applied to its output; C09 fixes the descriptive record published with it. C08's share is the only quantity C02 judges; no adjusted variant exists under this spec.

evidence.description: The withheld data file: 5,679 inscriptions, 77 sites, 2,717 Harappa (census pinned at freeze)
PRED-2026-006: the registered computation the share reproduces

claims.text: The per-sign table is published with the outcome as a descriptive record.
claims.boundary: The descriptive-record claim. It governs the one pre-registered addition to the registered computation: the per-sign table. The table is descriptive only. It does not govern the score (C08) or the verdict (C02), and no reading of the table moves either. The table lists every trained sign, its Harappa count, and its start rate.
alternatives: The per-sign table may be used after the fact to argue a different verdict than the registered share gives.
falsification_tests: One Spec 032 outcome missing the per-sign table, or one verdict argued from the table against the share, defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: The per-sign table may be used after the fact to argue a different verdict than the registered share gives.
metadata.verdict_rule: The table accompanies the outcome for reader inspection; the verdict rests on the share alone (C02, C08).
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C09 governs the descriptive table; C08 governs the score; C02 governs the verdict. C09's table can inform a reader and a future design; it cannot re-judge this run, and its pre-registration here is what keeps it from becoming a criterion. C09 and C04 share the outcome boundary: the table accompanies a computed outcome; a step-0 closure under C04 is reported as a closure, and the table neither supplies nor softens it. C09 and C07 are separate reporting statements (the table; the coverage line) and neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Design D-30 method section: the per-sign table pre-registered as descriptive

claims.text: The verdict wording claims only the site-withholding independence the registration specified.
claims.boundary: The independence-wording claim. It bounds the independence language of the verdict to site-withholding (Harappa held out of training, C05). It does not restate the conclusion boundary (C01): C01 bounds what the verdict is about; C10 bounds the independence it may claim. Scholarly-lineage independence is not claimed, because the Yajnadevam compilation's object base is published-corpus material.
alternatives: A pass on withheld Harappa data licenses wording that claims independence from the training corpus's scholarly lineage.
falsification_tests: One Spec 032 verdict statement claiming lineage independence, or omitting the within-lineage limit, defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A pass on withheld Harappa data licenses wording that claims independence from the training corpus's scholarly lineage.
metadata.verdict_rule: Verdict wording names the withholding as the independence held, and names the within-lineage limit in the same statement.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C10 bounds the independence wording; C01 bounds the conclusion's subject; C05 supplies the verified withholding fact C10's wording rests on. C10 neither widens C01 nor substitutes for C05's verification.

evidence.description: Design D-30 controls section: the within-lineage caution stated in the verdict wording
PRED-2026-006 withheld-data specification: site-withholding is the independence the registration defines

claims.text: The outcome is appended to the PRED register as a dated entry at execution.
claims.boundary: The register-handling claim. It governs how the outcome enters the program record (append-only, dated, at execution). It does not govern the verdict itself (C02) and it performs no register change at this freeze: the freeze leaves every register byte as it stands. The register's existing text stays byte-identical.
alternatives: Scoring a prediction licenses editing its register entry in place so the entry reads as always having carried the outcome.
falsification_tests: One edited (not appended) register byte attributable to Spec 032 defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Scoring a prediction licenses editing its register entry in place so the entry reads as always having carried the outcome.
metadata.verdict_rule: The register gains one dated appended entry per outcome; a byte diff of the pre-existing register text at execution shows no change.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C11 governs the record of the outcome; C02 governs the outcome; C12 governs how closures (which are also appended under C11) are worded. C11 changes nothing at freeze time and constrains the single append at execution time.

evidence.description: The register's own append discipline: outcomes appended as dated entries; the section 6 note of 2026-10-12 is the recorded precedent

claims.text: Step-0 closures are reported in closure vocabulary only.
claims.boundary: The closure-reporting claim. It governs the wording of the two soft landings the design allows. It does not govern when a closure triggers (C04 for the trained set; C05's verification for the withholding) or the verdict mapping that applies when no closure triggers (C02). The closures are CANNOT BE RUN AS WRITTEN and the UNMAPPABLE coverage statement.
alternatives: A step-0 closure may be reported as a partial confirmation, since the neighbouring global figure points the same way.
falsification_tests: One Spec 032 closure reported in verdict vocabulary defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A step-0 closure may be reported as a partial confirmation, since the neighbouring global figure points the same way.
metadata.verdict_rule: A closed study's outcome line is its closure, with its reason; the words CONFIRMED and NOT CONFIRMED appear only for a computed share.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C12 governs closure wording; C04 governs the trained-set closure trigger; C07 governs the coverage statement that accompanies either a verdict or a closure. C12 keeps closures and verdicts in separate vocabularies; it does not decide which occurs.

evidence.description: Design D-30 criteria section: the soft landings are reported as themselves, not dressed as verdicts
